prompt: Write the checks that separate a correct string reverser from three broken ones. Complete isCorrect in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Every one of these implementations returns "cba" for "abc", so the obvious happy-path assertion proves nothing at all. The empty string is the classic boundary that turns a wrong answer into a thrown StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, and only a checker that catches Throwable can score that as a failure instead of blowing up itself. The repeated-character case shows why fixtures should not be accidentally special: a string of distinct characters hides a bug that collapses duplicates.
hints: Reversing "abc" is passed by every implementation here, including the broken ones. You need inputs where the bugs actually change the answer.
Three boundary inputs pay off: the empty string "", a single character "a", and a string with a repeated letter such as "aba" or "noon".
Wrap the whole sequence of calls in try/catch and return false from the catch block -- an implementation that throws on "" has not met the contract.
